loraExtract.about1: Given an original model and a fine-tuned version of it, this computes what changed and stores it as a LoRA, which is far smaller than the full model.
loraExtract.about2: Rank controls how much detail is kept. Higher rank captures more of the difference at the cost of file size; 32 is a reasonable starting point. Valid range is 1 to 320.
loraExtract.about3: Both models must share an architecture. Extraction is GPU-heavy and can take several minutes.

loraExtract.sameModel: Pick two different models — comparing a model to itself produces nothing.

loraExtract.tunedModelHelp: The fine-tuned model to compare against the base.
loraExtract.warning: Requires a running backend with enough VRAM to hold both models. The result is only meaningful if the two models share a base architecture.

tokenizer.about1: Text encoders don't read words, they read tokens. A prompt that looks short can use more tokens than expected, and anything past a chunk boundary is processed separately. Every current Stable Diffusion model shares this same CLIP token set, so the result applies to all of them.
tokenizer.about2a: Each block shows the text-piece and, below it, its numeric token ID — the actual value handed to the encoder. Green blocks end a word (the encoder's
tokenizer.about2b: marker, meaning a space or punctuation follows); yellow blocks are word-pieces that run straight into the next block.
tokenizer.about3: Token IDs are useful for spotting when a word you thought was one concept is really several unrelated pieces, and for matching a token against embedding or vocabulary tooling that works in IDs rather than text.
tokenizer.defaultText: a photorealistic portrait of a tabby cat
tokenizer.example.skip1: a cat <lora:add_detail:0.8>  →  on: 2 tokens / off: 14 tokens
tokenizer.example.skip2: a <random:red|bright blue> car  →  on: 4 tokens / off: 10 tokens
tokenizer.example.skip3: a cat <segment:face> a face  →  on: 2 tokens / off: 11 tokens
tokenizer.example.weighting1: a (cat:1.5) on a mat  →  on: 5 tokens (cat @1.5) / off: 11 tokens
tokenizer.parseWeightingHelp: On, (word:1.5) syntax is read as a weight: the parentheses and the number vanish from the token stream and the word carries the weight instead. Off, every one of those characters is tokenized as literal text, which is what a model without weighting support would see.
tokenizer.stripSyntaxHelp: On, SwarmUI's own <...> prompt syntax is resolved before tokenizing: <lora:>, <embed:> and similar drop out entirely, <random:> and <wildcard:> collapse to their longest option, and everything from <segment:>, <object:>, <region:>, <clear:> or <extend:> onward is cut, since those are separate passes. Off, all of it is tokenized as plain text. Turn this on to see the count your model will actually receive.
tokenizer.summary: See exactly how a text encoder splits your prompt into tokens.
tokenizer.typeSomething: Type something above to tokenize it.
tokenizer.wordEndHint: Ends a word — a word break (space or punctuation) follows this token.
tokenizer.wordPieceHint: Word-piece — no word break after it, it connects directly to the next token.
